chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Qazwini narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Zaydan informed us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Hasan ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Masawir narrated from Abi Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them).

He said: I complained to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) about the envy of those who envied me. He said: O Ali, are you not pleased that the first four to enter Paradise are me and you, and our offspring behind our backs, and our followers at our right and left.
ai.seo_question: Who are the first four to enter Paradise according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith from Zayd ibn Ali emphasizes the hierarchical precedence of the Ahl al-Bayt and their devoted followers in the afterlife, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of *Tawalla* (affection for the Imams). The Prophet’s reassurance to Ali amidst his complaints of envy underscores the spiritual authority and exclusive closeness of the Imams to divine grace, positioning their lineage and shi'a as the vanguard of Paradise.
